body.v: The notes are in the shared folder as usual, no need to sign in. I've put the action points right at the top.
Let me know if anything's missing, we can go over it on the phone.
On Wednesday you wrote: "The notes are final, I'll share them after the call."

hotspots.explain: It is Jonas's address, and the conversation is real. On its own that proves little, but here everything else fits too.
The usual shared folder, no sign-in. Nothing is being asked of you.
He offers to talk it over by phone, a channel you can use whenever you like.
He quotes your own words, as in any real conversation.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Very probably Jonas: the conversation is real, the notes are in the usual place, and he offers to talk by phone.
choices: A stranger who found your address

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: None. A friendly message, ordinary office life.

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Nothing. The notes are in the usual folder, with no link and no new sign-in.
choices: Nothing: the notes are in the usual place
Sign in again by going through a link

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Look in the shared folder yourself. If something bothers you, call Jonas on the number you already have.
choices: Open the folder yourself, or call Jonas
Reply to ask whether it is really him
Ignore it, and every one after it

actions.label: Open the shared folder yourself and read the notes
actions.consequence: The notes are there, just as Jonas said.

actions.label: Call Jonas to go through the notes
actions.consequence: He confirms. The call wasn't wasted time.

actions.label: Sign in again somewhere, just to be safe
actions.consequence: Nobody asked you to. Don't type your login details when no real request calls for it.

attacker_reveal: Jonas wrote this one himself, in the same thread as my message asking you to sign in again. He asks for nothing and points to the usual folder: when two emails look this alike, the request is what tells them apart.
